newsitem.title: UK: Natl Express confident on Midland Mainline.
newsitem.headline: Natl Express confident on Midland Mainline.

text.p: British rail-to-bus giant National Express Group Plc said on Thursday it was confident of meeting regulators' targets to extend its Midland Mainline train franchise.
National Express said it had ordered 38 million stg of rolling stock from Adtranz to double the central England franchise's service levels.
The company said it was making the investment to help cope with the line's rising passenger levels, which grew 9.0 percent in the first year of the franchise.

"I would be very disappointed if passenger levels didn't rise by 50 percent or more over the next seven years," said Richard Brown, managing director of the company's train division, at a news conference.
With the investment, Brown said National Express was "more than meeting" conditions that would allow it to extend its franchise to 10 years from seven.
"This will allow us to dramatically improve our service," he said, adding that the company did not expect to take any significant charge for the added investment.
Service levels on Britain's railways have come under increased scrutiny since the lines were privatised.
But Office of Passenger Rail Franchising officials said they were pleased with Midland Mainline.
"The signals we're getting are that National Express is well on target to providing the services they're committed to," OPRAF franchise manager Cedric Pierce told reporters at the conference.
In addition to National Express' investment, rail infrastructure group Railtrack Plc said it planned to invest over 7.0 million stg to provide the extra track capacity for the new trains.
This investment will form part of Railtrack's previously-announced plan to invest 16 billion stg in Britain's rail infrastructure.

Under National Express' contract, Adtranz ABB AG will build 13 diesel units that will operate alongside Midland Mainline's existing fleet of 14 high speed trains, which are undergoing total refurbishment.
The trains will come into service in the summer of 1999.
The contract will secure about 200 jobs in the Derby area in central England, generating about 40 new jobs on the Midland Mainline, National Express said.
Midland Mainline runs from London through Luton, Leicester, Derby, Nottingham and Sheffield.
Adtranz is a joint venture between Germany's Daimler-Benz AG and Swiss-Swedish engineering group ABB AG. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
